description: Bidirectional REBOUND/DE440s replication of the transit channel on the third (one-apparition, J/A+A/571/A63) catalogue, with the bipolar slip map fitted on the 229 Warsaw+CODE comets applied out-of-sample.  Axis: cap-declaration (34,-13); detached-sample (49.9,-17) scored as second anchor.  MW08 comparison is 1/a-only (energy channel) by construction of the MW08 record.

verdict.reading: The third catalogue (one-apparition, n=30) was run through the identical bidirectional instrument: simulated boundary legs reproduce the catalogue's own original/future solutions to 0.0000 deg median (p95 0.0015 deg).  Its unexplained slip decreases with transit angle at rho -0.367 (p=0.046; negative rho is the TEP direction, matching the -0.32 of the CODE cohort), with in-cap vs out-cap medians +3.69 vs -3.95 yr (p=0.043).  23 members also carry near-identical Warsaw/CODE solutions (the same orbit record); on that subset the decline persists at rho -0.418.  The bipolar map fitted on the 229 Warsaw+CODE comets predicts this cohort at rho +0.115 (p=0.543), sign 17/30 -- positive but unresolved at n=30.

caveats: The lpc cohort is not disjoint in membership or in solution: 23 of 30 members also carry Warsaw/CODE entries inside the 229-comet training set, and on shared members the two catalogues' three-leg rotations agree to ~0.001 deg (measured at rho=0.999 in step 106) -- the same underlying orbit record republished with uncertainties and the MW08 comparison, not an independent re-fit.  The genuinely new information is the 7 members absent from the training set plus the instrument validation itself.  The cohort shares the Poznan orbit-determination lineage; the MW08 lineage contributes only the 1/a energy channel (no angular elements published).
n=30 after the spike cut; the transfer test is powered for consistency, not detection.
dtau_unexplained here is detrended within the lpc cohort itself (same covariates as step 065); the map prediction uses the 229-fitted coefficients, so the two detrendings are independent.
